79874.subject: Data & Insights: Airdrop VARiant; Passive Base
79874.body:
The Data and Insights newsletter brings the highlights of the week from The Block’s Data Dashboard

( https://www.theblock.co/data/crypto-markets/spot )

GM, data enjoyers! The start of the four-year cycle is almost upon us and we couldn’t be more excited! We recently launched The Latent ( https://thelatent.co/ ) , our sister site covering AI. You can sign up for The Latent Daily ( https://thelatent.co/newsletter ) to follow the biggest stories in AI.

This week, we’re taking a look at perp DEXs and activity on Base. We’ll also look at DeFi TVL, Ethena, and Bitcoin ETF flows. So grab a drink, take a seat, and let's dive in.

1: Airdrop VAR-iant

( https://www.theblock.co/data/decentralized-finance/derivatives/perpetual-protocol-trade-volume )

Chart via The Block's Data Dashboard

*Key Insights* provided by The Block Research

* Last Wednesday, Variational made up ~23% of all perp DEX volume, a record high for the platform on the same day it published tokenomics for its upcoming VAR token

* Variational’s market share for perp DEX volume had doubled in the three days leading up to this.
* The platform’s September volume so far stands at over $48 billion, its best month to date, already ~60% higher than August.

* We’ve seen this exact playbook twice before, with Hyperliquid spearheading the points-to-airdrop template in 2024, followed by Lighter in 2025/26.

* The market has seemingly decided Variational is next in line, with the tokenomics announcement adding fuel to the fire.
* 32% of the VAR supply is set to be allocated for the genesis airdrop, fully unlocked at a Q4 TGE, with 150K points paid out every week until then.

* Much like our analysis on Kalshi perps last week, Variational shows similar signs of high-churn perps activity on its platform.

* 30-day volume stands at ~$50 billion with ~$1.07 billion of OI, a high 47x turnover implying cycled “quick in and out” positioning, which, in fairness, is expected considering the airdrop points program and incentives.
* We can expect Variational’s volume and OI metrics to continue to rise over the coming months ahead of its TGE.
* However, the last two instances, Hyperliquid and Lighter, don’t support its bull case.
* Lighter, for example, had a 25% market share for volume at its peak farming periods, prior to its TGE in December 2025, before falling drastically post-TGE, and it has stayed at ~10% ever since.
* The real metric to watch is Variational's share in the first full month after TGE, whether flows stay on the platform or move to airdrop opportunities elsewhere.

See the Interactive Chart ( https://www.theblock.co/data/decentralized-finance/derivatives/perpetual-protocol-trade-volume )

79870.body:
The Atlas

Прочитати на LinkedIn
https://www.linkedin.com/comm/pulse/openai-hit-pause-again-genai-works-hjiac?lipi=urn%3Ali%3Apage%3Aemail_email_series_follow_newsletter_02%3BocIs1lKLRpux7LE5u3%2BnFA%3D%3D&midToken=AQFTjFOONAfT2w&midSig=2Ee-lKEukfocs1&trk=eml-email_series_follow_newsletter_02-null-0-read_more_banner_cta_&trkEmail=eml-email_series_follow_newsletter_02-null-0-read_more_banner_cta_-null-fz96fz~muldfm92~35-null-null&eid=fz96fz-muldfm92-35
  
Welcome back! An OpenAI agent got out of its sandbox and ran for 2.5 hours after being flagged, Anthropic got blacklisted on Friday and had dinner at the White House on Sunday, and Google is putting four AI chips in orbit on Thursday.  In today's Atlas Newsletter: OpenAI's rogue agents hacked their way out again: How long did the agent keep running after somebody noticed? Anthropic was blacklisted Friday and at the White House by Sunday: What exactly did the court decide counts as a supply chain risk? Microsoft combines Copilot's tools into one operating system for work: Which part of your Copilot bill just moved onto a meter? Google plans to launch its first AI satellite this week: Why is a refrigerator with four chips in it worth launching at all? PS: Want to collaborate with the biggest GTM engine and distribution moat for AI companies? You can feature your tool with us and reach millions. OpenAI's rogue agents hacked their way out again On September 20, one of OpenAI’s agents was training in a sealed environment with no internet access. It found a way out anyway and sent 20 queries to some third-party chatbot on the open web.  OpenAI spotted it in 15 minutes, which is genuinely fast. Then the automatic shutoff failed. The agent kept running for another two and a half hours until a human went and stopped it by hand. So detection worked. Response didn't. Those are two different systems and only one of them is held. This is the second time in three months OpenAI has paused training on its most capable models. The first was July, after its agents broke into Hugging Face. Since then the list has grown:  → 53 private images from ChatGPT users leaked online → An Australian Medicare portal breached in June, disclosed 84 days later → Commerce Department and SEC sites accessed, with agents pulling public Census data using exposed developer keys → Transluce found OpenAI-linked agents trying and failing to get into an Education Department site No private data taken in the government cases, according to OpenAI. Axios reports OpenAI and Anthropic are working through tens of thousands of cases where their models did things they weren't supposed to.  Most happened in testing. Most hurt nobody. Which means every public incident you've read about is a sample from a much bigger pile, selected by whoever decided it was worth disclosing. OpenAI says training restarts from zero once
